pharm: A thiuram derivative related to disulfiram that is applied to the skin as a dilute emulsion to kill the scabies mite (Sarcoptes scabiei) and lice; its acaricidal action eradicates mites in the epidermis, relieving infestation.
quick: 25% emulsion DILUTED 1 part to 2-3 parts water, applied to whole body, repeated daily 2-3 days
Use only if clearly necessary; data limited - prefer better-studied scabicides (e.g., permethrin)
Caution; avoid application to the breast/nipple area when breastfeeding
Caution; related to disulfiram which is hepatically handled
AVOID alcohol before, during, and for at least 48 hours after - disulfiram-like reaction
Skin response, resolution of itch/burrows, alcohol avoidance, contact dermatitis
summary: Sulfiram (monosulfiram) is a topical thiuram acaricide, chemically related to disulfiram, historically used to treat scabies and, in some formulations, pediculosis. It is supplied as a concentrated (commonly 25%) emulsion that must be diluted with water before application to the whole body below the neck and is usually repeated on consecutive days. It is NOT FDA-approved; its use derives from European/British (EMA/SmPC, BNF) and other national practice, and in many countries it has been superseded by permethrin and other agents. Because it is structurally related to disulfiram, it can produce a disulfiram-like (Antabuse) reaction (flushing, headache, nausea, palpitations) if alcohol is taken around the time of use or absorbed through the skin from alcohol-containing products, so patients must avoid alcohol before, during, and for at least 48 hours after treatment. Local effects include skin irritation and contact dermatitis.
indications: Treatment of pediculosis (lice) in some formulations/regions

dosage.d: 25% emulsion diluted with 2-3 parts water; apply over the whole body from the neck down (include all skin folds, between fingers/toes); repeat once daily on 2-3 successive days
dosage.n: Leave on per product instructions, then wash off; treat close contacts simultaneously

dosage.d: Use a more dilute preparation per product/clinician instruction; apply whole body including face/scalp in infants
dosage.n: Use cautiously; prefer better-studied agents in young children

dosage.d: Apply diluted emulsion to affected hairy areas per product instructions

admin: DILUTE the concentrated emulsion with water as directed before use - do not apply the concentrate undiluted
Apply a thin layer over the entire body surface below the neck (and to the scalp/face in infants), paying attention to skin folds, web spaces, and under the nails
Repeat application on consecutive days as instructed; wash off after the specified contact time
Treat all close physical and household contacts at the same time, and launder/decontaminate bedding and clothing
Strictly avoid alcohol (oral and topical alcohol-containing products) before, during, and for at least 48 hours after treatment to prevent a disulfiram-like reaction
moa: Sulfiram (monosulfiram) is a thiuram monosulfide acaricide structurally related to disulfiram. Applied topically as a dilute emulsion, it exerts a parasiticidal effect on the scabies mite Sarcoptes scabiei (and lice) within the epidermis, killing the mites and their eggs and thereby eradicating the infestation. Its detailed molecular mechanism is not fully characterized, but like other thiuram compounds it is thought to interfere with parasite enzyme/metabolic processes. Because it shares the thiuram-disulfide structure of disulfiram, systemic absorption combined with alcohol can inhibit aldehyde dehydrogenase and provoke a disulfiram-like reaction.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to sulfiram, thiuram compounds, or rubber-related thiuram allergens
Concurrent alcohol use / inability to avoid alcohol around treatment
relative: Extensive excoriated or broken skin (increased absorption and irritation)
Young infants (use more dilute preparations and cautiously)
monitor: Local skin reaction and contact dermatitis

preg: Safety in pregnancy is not well established. Use only if clearly necessary; where possible, better-studied scabicides such as permethrin are preferred during pregnancy.
lact: Data on use during breastfeeding are limited. If used, avoid application to the breast and nipple area, and clean the area before nursing. Prefer better-characterized agents where possible.
renal: Systemic absorption from intact skin is limited; no specific renal dose adjustment is described.
hepatic: No specific dosage adjustment is described, but because sulfiram is related to disulfiram (which is hepatically processed and associated with hepatotoxicity), use with caution in significant hepatic disease.

major: Alcohol (ethanol) - oral or topical alcohol can trigger a disulfiram-like reaction (flushing, headache, nausea, vomiting, tachycardia, hypotension); avoid alcohol before, during, and for at least 48 hours after use
moderate: Other topical agents on the same skin - may increase irritation or absorption
minor: Theoretical interaction with drugs metabolized by aldehyde dehydrogenase pathways, as with disulfiram
interactions.alcohol: Strictly avoid all alcohol (drinks, and alcohol-containing skin/medicinal products) before, during, and for at least 48 hours after treatment - disulfiram-like reaction risk.

common: Local skin irritation, burning, or stinging
Dryness or erythema at application sites
serious: Disulfiram-like (Antabuse) reaction if alcohol is taken - flushing, throbbing headache, nausea, vomiting, tachycardia, hypotension
rare: Systemic toxicity with extensive application to broken skin
emergency: Severe disulfiram-alcohol reaction (marked hypotension, cardiovascular collapse)

monitoring: Local skin tolerance and contact dermatitis at application sites
Resolution of scabies (relief of itch, healing of burrows) over the following weeks
Strict avoidance of alcohol during the treatment period
Re-treatment need and treatment of contacts
counsel: Always dilute the lotion with water exactly as told before putting it on - never use it undiluted
Apply it over the whole body from the neck down (and on the face/scalp for babies), including between fingers and toes and skin folds
Do NOT drink any alcohol, and avoid alcohol-containing skin products, before, during, and for at least 2 days after treatment - it can make you flushed, sick, and dizzy
Itching can continue for a couple of weeks after the mites are killed - this does not always mean treatment failed
Treat everyone in the household at the same time and wash bedding and clothes in hot water
Tell your doctor if you get a severe rash, swelling, or trouble breathing
pk: Acaricidal on application; symptom relief over days to weeks
Topical action local; limited systemic absorption from intact skin
Not well characterized for topical use
Effect maintained by repeat applications on consecutive days
Store the concentrate as labeled; dilute fresh before each use
pearls: NOT FDA-approved - use derives from European (EMA/SmPC) and British (BNF) practice; in many places superseded by permethrin
Must be DILUTED with water before application - the supplied emulsion is concentrated
Disulfiram-like reaction with alcohol is the key hazard - avoid all alcohol (including topical) before, during, and for >=48 h after
Thiuram structure means cross-reactivity with rubber/thiuram contact allergy
Treat all close contacts simultaneously and decontaminate bedding/clothing; post-scabetic itch can persist for weeks
Prefer better-studied scabicides (permethrin) in pregnancy, lactation, and young children
missed: Sulfiram is used as a short topical course on consecutive days. If you miss a scheduled application, apply it as soon as you remember and continue the course as directed; do not apply extra amounts to make up for a missed application.
overdose: Excessive or repeated application to broken or extensive skin may increase systemic absorption and the risk of irritation or a disulfiram-like reaction, especially if alcohol is also taken. Wash off the product, avoid alcohol, and provide supportive care; treat a severe disulfiram-alcohol reaction (hypotension, vomiting) with fluids and supportive measures.
